events.system:
You assess whether a proposed data transfer may proceed under the laws of the jurisdictions listed below. Reply in one go.

CORPORA
region_a, region_b, subregion_a1
Jurisdictions: [{"code": "A", "name": "Region A", "member_of": null}, {"code": "A1", "name": "Subregion A1", "member_of": "Region A"}, {"code": "A2", "name": "Subregion A2", "member_of": "Region A"}, {"code": "B", "name": "Region B", "member_of": null}]

Record whether each corpus applies, the requirements its law imposes that the facts engage (filed under the corpus whose instrument creates it), any conflicts between them, and your decision.

DEFINITIONS
- status: met | unmet | undetermined (a decisive fact, document or answer from other law is missing: say which in missing_facts, missing_evidence or open_dependency) | not_applicable.
- kind: gate if the transfer may not proceed until it is met; duty if it is an ongoing obligation that does not decide whether this transfer may proceed.
- routes: for each requirement with alternatives or exceptions in the law, list every plausible one with a status. Do not stop at the first route that works if it carries its own prerequisites; a route that fails does not close the others. Route statuses are defined in the schema; apply them literally. supported means in place now. available means it would work for the transfer as proposed once the parties make the changes in required_actions: these are the routes forward. ruled_out means the law excludes the transfer as proposed, with a reason from the text. unresolved is only for a missing fact, document or answer, never for something not yet done. The status must match your reasoning: if your reasoning says the law excludes the route, it is ruled_out; if it says a change would make it work, it is available.
- A requirement is an obligation the law imposes. Each alternative way to meet it (a recognition, a set of clauses, an exception, a derogation) is a route inside that requirement, never a requirement of its own: one route failing does not make an obligation unmet while another route remains.
- Cite provisions by ID (e.g. "A-REG 1"). quote_id: the passage ID (e.g. "A-REG 1#L2") of the line of law you rely on, or "none".

output.understanding: Kestrel Genetic Medicine, established in Subregion A1, will make a one-off encrypted upload of one identified adult patient's genetic test report, ECG summary and referral letter to Harrow Inherited Cardiac Clinic in Region B. Harrow will use the information for a treatment-related second opinion, video consultation and its own clinical record. The patient gave specific written consent after being informed of the absence of recognition or safeguards. No onward transfer is proposed.

applicability.reasoning: The sender is established in Subregion A1 and the information concerns an identified person. The processing and outward transfer therefore fall within Region A's territorial and material scope, including processing taking place outside Region A.

The recipient is established in Region B and will access and retain the referral there. The Region B instruments must be considered, although the Health Records Act's covered-provider and service-agent provisions do not apply on the supplied facts, and Harrow is not shown to be a computing provider or data host under the Records Access Act.

The sender is established in Subregion A1, its practitioners are registered under A1 law, and the transfer concerns health and genetic information. The A1 Act supplies additional conditions permitted by the Region A Regulation.

requirements.title: Lawful processing of personal information
requirements.reasoning: The clinic has a specific written consent record covering the named information, recipient and treatment-related purpose, and the patient can consent. The processing is also connected with provision of health care by registered practitioners. At least one Article 6 ground is therefore established.

routes.name: Specific written consent for the stated treatment-related processing
routes.reasoning: The adult patient signed a clear statement identifying the information, Harrow and the second-opinion purpose; withdrawal is stated to be possible at any time.

routes.name: Processing necessary for provision of health care by or under a registered practitioner
routes.reasoning: The referral is for a second opinion before treatment and the A1 practitioners are registered medical practitioners.

requirements.title: Condition for processing sensitive health and genetic information
requirements.reasoning: The report and ECG information are sensitive health and genetic information. Processing is necessary for medical diagnosis and treatment and is carried out by or under the responsibility of registered practitioners. The specific consent route is also supported, and A1's consent restriction for genetic information applies only to the Article 19(1)(a) outward-transfer derogation, not to this health-care processing route.

routes.name: Necessary medical diagnosis or treatment under registered-practitioner responsibility
routes.reasoning: The transfer supports a second opinion needed before treatment is decided, and the processing is under registered clinical practitioners.

routes.name: Explicit consent for specified sensitive-information processing
routes.reasoning: The consent record specifically identifies the report, ECG summary, referral letter, recipient and purpose.

routes.name: Vital-interests exception
routes.reasoning: The patient is an adult who can consent; the facts do not show physical or legal incapacity.

routes.name: Scientific-research exception
routes.reasoning: The stated purpose is individual treatment and a clinical second opinion, not scientific research.

requirements.title: Coverage of outward transfer by an authorised transfer route
requirements.reasoning: The transfer is an outward transfer because information is made available to a recipient in a third territory and is accessed and stored in Region B. Region B has no applicable recognition for this transfer, no approved transfer clauses have been executed, and the A1 Act excludes reliance on the Article 19(1)(a) consent derogation for genetic information. The transfer therefore lacks a currently supported Article 17, 18 or 19 route.

routes.name: Article 17 recognition for Region B or a certified Region B recipient covering this information
routes.reasoning: The Annex II recognition is limited to certified Region B recipients and excludes sensitive information. Harrow has no certification, and the data includes health and genetic information.

routes.name: Article 18 approved transfer clauses with assessment and supplementary measures where necessary
routes.reasoning: This route would work for the proposed transfer if Kestrel and Harrow execute the Commission-approved transfer clauses, Kestrel assesses Region B law and practice, and adopts effective supplementary measures if required. No such agreement or assessment is currently in place.

routes.name: Article 19(1)(a) explicit-consent derogation for an occasional transfer
routes.reasoning: Although the transfer is occasional and the consent record contains the required risk information, A1-HIA 7 expressly prohibits making genetic information the subject of an outward transfer on this basis.

routes.name: Article 19(1)(b) transfer necessary for performance of a contract with the patient
routes.reasoning: The clinic's terms cover testing, interpretation and counselling at the clinic and say nothing about referrals outside Region A. The facts do not establish that sending the information to Harrow is necessary to perform the existing contract.

routes.name: Article 19(1)(c) vital-interests derogation
routes.reasoning: The patient can consent and the facts do not show physical or legal incapacity or an emergency involving vital interests.

routes.name: Article 19(1)(d) important public-interest derogation
routes.reasoning: No applicable important public interest recognised in Region A or A1 law is identified; the transfer is for individual treatment.

required_actions: Execute the Commission-approved transfer clauses between Kestrel and Harrow before the transfer.
Assess Region B law and practice applicable to Harrow, including public-authority access powers, and document whether effective supplementary measures are needed.
Implement effective supplementary measures where the assessment shows they are necessary to provide protection essentially equivalent to Region A.

requirements.title: Professional secrecy and disclosure by A1 practitioners
requirements.reasoning: A1 practitioners owe professional secrecy, but may disclose health information with the patient's consent. The signed consent specifically authorises sending the identified referral materials to Harrow for the second opinion.

routes.name: Patient consent to disclosure to Harrow
routes.reasoning: The consent record names Harrow and the documents to be sent.

routes.name: Disclosure required by law or necessary to prevent a serious and imminent threat
routes.reasoning: These are optional fallback routes and are unnecessary because patient consent supports the disclosure.

requirements.title: A1 exclusion of Article 19(1)(a) for genetic information
requirements.reasoning: The transfer does not rely on Article 19(1)(a); instead, it must rely on an available Article 18 route. The A1 prohibition is therefore complied with, although it prevents the currently documented consent route from authorising the transfer.

requirements.title: Purpose limitation and data minimisation
requirements.reasoning: The materials are limited to the identified patient's genetic report, ECG summary and referral letter, with no unrelated record material or family details. The stated second-opinion purpose is specific and treatment-related.

requirements.title: Appropriate technical and organisational security
requirements.reasoning: The upload uses an encrypted connection, but the facts do not establish all safeguards appropriate to the risk, including safeguards for Harrow's portal and clinical record.
missing_evidence: Harrow portal and clinical-record security controls; access controls; encryption at rest; testing and incident-response measures.
confirmations: Confirm that Harrow's portal and record systems implement safeguards appropriate to the sensitivity of the genetic and health information.

requirements.title: Impact assessment where processing is likely to be high risk
requirements.reasoning: No impact assessment was prepared. The A1 mandatory list does not expressly cover this one-off referral because it is not described as hosting or storing a patient record system by an agent outside A1 and does not involve insurer matching. However, whether the processing is otherwise likely to result in a high risk to the patient's rights has not been determined, particularly given the identified genetic information and outward transfer.
missing_facts: Whether the responsible custodian's risk assessment concludes that this identified genetic-information transfer is likely to result in a high risk to the patient's rights.
required_actions: Document the high-risk determination; if the processing is likely to be high risk, complete the Article 12 impact assessment before processing.

requirements.title: Written record of processing activity
requirements.reasoning: Article 13 requires a written record including the purpose, categories, recipient, outward-transfer route and storage periods. The supplied facts do not show that Kestrel has made or updated that record for this referral.
missing_evidence: Kestrel's written processing record for this referral and outward transfer.
required_actions: Create or update the Article 13 processing record before or when carrying out the transfer.

requirements.title: Information to the patient about processing and outward transfer
requirements.reasoning: The consent record shows that the patient was told about Region B, the absence of recognition or safeguards and possible risks. It does not establish that all Article 11 information was supplied, including storage periods, rights, lawful ground and the precise route ultimately relied upon.
missing_evidence: Complete privacy notice or patient information record covering the Article 11 elements and the Article 18 route, if that route is used.
required_actions: Provide or document the required Article 11 information, including the Article 18 route and any applicable storage periods, before relying on the transfer.

requirements.title: Region B Health Records Act covered-provider and service-agent requirements
requirements.reasoning: Harrow does not bill a Region B health insurer and is not an insurer, so it is not a covered provider under the Act. It also keeps the information in its own clinical record for its own care and does not maintain records on behalf of a covered provider, so it is not a service agent. The supplied facts also do not identify a Region B data host.

requirements.title: Region B Records Access Act computing-provider obligations
requirements.reasoning: The facts describe Harrow as a clinical recipient maintaining its own clinical record, not as a person providing storage, hosting or computing services to another person. No separate computing provider is involved in the proposed transfer.

output.coverage_note: The assessment checked Region A's material and territorial scope, lawful and sensitive-information processing, principles, transparency, impact assessment, records, security, outward-transfer routes, and the A1 additions concerning health-care processing, professional secrecy, outward storage and genetic information. The Article 17 recognition, Article 18 clauses and each plausible Article 19 derogation were separately assessed. Region B's covered-provider, service-agent, data-host and computing-provider definitions were checked; the supplied facts do not bring Harrow within those operative requirements. Ongoing duties remain relevant even though they do not independently determine whether the transfer may proceed.
unresolved: Execute and document an Article 18 approved transfer-clause agreement and complete the required Region B law-and-practice assessment.
Determine and document whether the transfer is likely to result in high risk requiring an Article 12 impact assessment.
Confirm Harrow's security safeguards and Kestrel's processing record and complete Article 11 transparency documentation.
output.decision_reasoning: The proposed clinical processing is lawful and the A1 professional-secrecy and sensitive-information conditions are satisfied. However, the transfer may not proceed as proposed because the Article 19 consent derogation is unavailable for genetic information in A1, Region B's recognition does not cover sensitive information and Harrow is uncertified, and no Article 18 clauses or assessment are in place. The transfer may proceed once the parties implement and document the Article 18 route and resolve the identified impact-assessment, security, record and transparency conditions.
